pages.text: $(bold)Cursed Spirit Manipulation$(): all things can be devoured, and every cursed spirit tamed.$(br2)$(bold)Forward · Subjugate$(): beat an $(bold)undead$() within your sight down to ≤ $(bold)2.5%$() health, then aim at it and press the release key — that $(bold)individual$() (not its species! including a $(bold)complete NBT snapshot$() of its held items, equipment, attributes and effects) is stored in the individual-list GUI, and its body dissolves into black particles (a boss fight ends outright).$(li)cost = ceil(max(1, max health/20 × (10 + Output × 4) × (1 - Affinity/100))) cursed energy$(li)after subjugating, you gain $(bold)30 seconds of Hunger$() and $(bold)10 seconds of Nausea$()$(br2)If the conditions are not met (not undead / health above the execution line / no target in sight), the individual-list GUI simply opens instead.

$(bold)Forward · Release / Recall$(): the GUI shows every individual in a scrolling list ($(bold)name + 3D entity preview$(), including its release state):$(li)click a captured individual → it is $(bold)released at full health$() in front of its master: the caster becomes its master, and it $(bold)ignores the caster and their teammates$(), automatically seeking out whoever attacks the caster or whoever the caster is attacking$(li)click a released individual again → recall it (its record is kept)$(li)if a released individual is slain in battle, its record is $(bold)lost forever$()$(br2)$(bold)Reversal · Sacrifice$(): pick an unreleased individual in the GUI — its data is wiped and it starts charging a vortex; $(bold)press the reversal key again$() to fire a $(bold)Black Vortex$() straight along your sight (spinning black smoke, similar in effect to Limitless' Hollow Purple).

$(bold)Black Vortex damage$(): D = $(bold)the sacrificed spirit's max health x 40%$(), $(bold)then multiplied by the Modular Staff's spell amplification$() — the former $(bold)scales with the max health of the individual you sacrificed$() (the 40% ratio is a constant), while the latter only looks at whether you are holding a staff with the "Modular Staff" trait in either hand $(bold)at the moment you fire$() (with no staff the amplification is x1): without amplification, sacrificing a Zombie (20 HP) deals about 8, a common undead at 150 HP about 60, a Wither (300 HP) about 120. It does $(bold)not$() scale with your Affinity/Output, nor with that individual's attack damage; once it hits or reaches its range, it falls off linearly over a 3-block radius, and the target's armour and damage reduction still apply.$(li)firing the vortex costs = ceil(M × 50) (M = 1 + (Output + Affinity/10)/10)$(br2)$(bold)Tip$(): the subjugation cost rises with the individual's max health — ordinary zombies are cheap, while boss-tier undead are pricey but can end a battle early; the 2.5% execution line also means you must first grind the target's health down to almost nothing.$(li)Because the vortex reads max health: $(bold)the tankier the undead you sacrifice, the harder it hits$() (a Wither, a Giant or any boss-tier undead far outclasses a Zombie) — but subjugating it costs proportionally more.
